events.extended_summary: Former Danish prime minister Anders Fogh Rasmussen, who served as NATO secretary-general from 2009 to 2014, accused Britain and France of presiding over a "coalition of the waiting" while Russia dragged out peace talks. The 73-year-old called for the immediate deployment of troops to Ukraine, arguing Europe should transform the "coalition of the willing" into a "coalition of the doing" without waiting for a peace deal. His remarks came during US-led negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine and Russia focused on security guarantees, from which European officials were excluded after Moscow objected. Rasmussen proposed a five-point strategy including extending NATO air and missile defence systems over western Ukraine, urging Germany, Spain and Greece to supply Patriot interceptors, and confiscating more than €200 billion in frozen Russian assets to fund Kyiv's defence.
events.micro_summary: Former Danish PM Anders Fogh Rasmussen urges Britain and France to deploy troops to Ukraine immediately.
events.summary: Former Danish prime minister and NATO chief Anders Fogh Rasmussen accused Britain and France of presiding over a "coalition of the waiting" and urged immediate troop deployment to Ukraine to push for peace during ongoing negotiations.

events.extended_summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he wanted a “lasting, permanent peace” in Ukraine while reiterating Moscow’s opposition to foreign troops on Ukrainian territory, during a Kremlin meeting with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Thursday, Nov. 12. Trump’s envoys arrived in Moscow on Thursday to brief Putin on the outcome of the recent trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi. As of 3:21 p.m. Kyiv time, the meeting between Putin, Witkoff, and Kushner had been underway for an hour. According to Russia’s state news agency TASS, Putin proposed organizing another humanitarian mission in Ukraine, this time from Kostyantynivka, following what he described as a successful humanitarian operation in Oleshky, in the occupied Kherson region. Putin claimed Russia controlled Kostyantynivka and was prepared to guarantee the safety of a humanitarian mission there. He said Moscow would need five days to clear mines around the city, adding that if Kyiv considered the

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused the Starshield military satellite system of being systematically restricted to 100 miles per hour (161 kilometres per hour) along the entire front line and in temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine. Zelensky stated that Ukrainian military investigations confirmed these are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions that have been ongoing for several days. The slowdown hampers Kyiv's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and has already allowed some strikes to hit Ukraine, which Zelensky said is helping Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes. The accusation came as US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow for peace talks. Starshield, developed by SpaceX for military use, plays a vital role in front-line communications. A similar connectivity issue affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before being resolved.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky says Starshield satellite speeds are limited to 100mph along the front line, hampering drone interception.

events.extended_summary: Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's US Senate race, defeating incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith with 49.2% of the vote to her 48.7%. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated the candidates. Colom, 43, became the first Black senator from Mississippi since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881, and the first Democratic senator elected in the state since 1982. The victory gives Democrats 55 seats in the 100-member Senate. Colom campaigned on a 'Mississippi Matters' platform, engaging voters at hair salons, colleges, and Trump rallies. He delivered a victory speech at Tougaloo College, while Hyde-Smith congratulated him in a video, respecting the voters' decision. The contest was not considered competitive until final weeks despite President Trump winning the state by more than 22 points in 2024.
events.micro_summary: Scott Colom won Mississippi's Senate seat with 49.2% of the vote, becoming the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction.
events.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's US Senate race with 49.2% to 48.7%, becoming the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction and the first Democrat elected there since 1982.

events.extended_summary: Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found. Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year. This level of warming smashes the 1.5C threshold that was agreed by countries a decade ago but is set to be breached in just a few years. Scientists have warned that beyond this point already harmful storms, droughts, heatwaves, flooding and other impacts will become intolerable for parts of the world
events.micro_summary: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns.
events.summary: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns. The world is heading for an "irrecoverable overshoot" on dangerous warming unless governments reject fossil fuels and start rapidly cutting emissions, a report has warned.

events.extended_summary: The SS United States, once the fastest ship in the world and longer than the Titanic, was intentionally sunk off the coast of Destin, Florida, on Wednesday, becoming the world's largest artificial ocean reef. The vessel spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before being moved to Alabama last year for cleaning, then making its final journey to Florida on Monday. Purchased by a Florida county, the ship will serve as a home for sealife and an underwater attraction, with a land-based museum planned to detail its history. The liner operated from 1952 to 1969, crossing the Atlantic hundreds of times and carrying royalty and celebrities including former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy, and a young Bill Clinton. Activists unsuccessfully fought to preserve the ship as a museum, and previous proposals for a floating hotel failed. The sinking was conducted as a precision operation without explosives.
events.micro_summary: The SS United States, once the world's fastest ship, was intentionally sunk off Florida as the world's largest artificial reef.
events.summary: The SS United States, a historic liner longer than the Titanic, was intentionally sunk off the coast of Destin, Florida, on Wednesday to become the world's largest artificial ocean reef after nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia.

events.extended_summary: Legendary sportscaster Dan Hicks died Wednesday at age 64 following an acute illness, his wife Hannah Storm announced in a statement. Hicks had been with NBC Sports since 1992, serving as the network's lead golf play-by-play announcer since 2000 and calling Notre Dame football, the Olympics, and the PGA Tour. Among his most famous broadcast moments were calling Tiger Woods' dramatic putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open and the U.S. swim team's comeback at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. He was married to Storm since January 1994 and was father to three daughters: Hannah, Ellery, and Riley. Colleagues described him as an exceptional storyteller who elevated major moments in sports history.
events.micro_summary: Legendary sportscaster Dan Hicks died at 64 following an acute illness, his wife Hannah Storm announced.

events.extended_summary: Racing Bulls have confirmed that Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue as drivers for the 2027 Formula 1 season. The decision was reached by team principal Alan Permane and Red Bull counterpart Laurent Mekies after deliberations over whether to retain Lawson or promote junior driver Nikola Tsolov. Lawson, 24, has scored points in 15 of the 20 grands prix this season and deputised at Red Bull for three races after Isack Hadjar fractured a wrist. He sits ninth in the drivers' standings, 47 points clear of Alpine's Pierre Gasly, and has helped Racing Bulls secure fifth in the constructors' standings, 45 points ahead of Alpine. The team's shareholders and Red Bull GmbH approved the decision despite Lawson receiving a one-place grid penalty for an altercation with Max Verstappen during Mexico City Grand Prix practice.
events.micro_summary: Racing Bulls confirm Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

events.extended_summary: The NFL trade deadline passed with the Minnesota Vikings acquiring quarterback Kirk Cousins for his second stint, while the Chiefs added Josh Downs. The Titans traded Jeffery Simmons for two first-round picks and Amani Hooker to the Bills for a second-rounder, while the Colts traded four players for one top-100 pick, keeping Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor. At midseason, AFC playoff teams are the Bills, Broncos, Jaguars, Steelers, Chiefs, Bengals, and Patriots; NFC teams are the 49ers, Bears, Giants, Panthers, Lions, Vikings, and Packers. Projections show all four NFC North teams reaching the playoffs for the first time in history. The Vikings are projected to finish 11-3 but third in their division, while the Patriots (5-4) hold the AFC's seventh seed over the Texans (3-5), both projected at 9-8.
events.micro_summary: Vikings acquire Kirk Cousins at NFL trade deadline as all four NFC North teams projected to reach playoffs.

events.extended_summary: A three-storey mixed-use building in New York City collapsed Wednesday afternoon at the edge of a construction site where workers were excavating an empty lot, killing at least eight people and injuring at least 17 others, including three firefighters. The building, which had apartments above ground-floor commercial space, fell while construction was underway next door, sending rubble into the construction pit. About 250 firefighters worked overnight using pickaxes, power saws, and search dogs to dig through the wreckage, pulling several survivors from the debris including a woman hoisted out on a stretcher Wednesday night. Among the dead was a 23-year-old construction worker whose body was recovered from the pit; his wife was described as hysterical at the scene. The cause remains under investigation, and heavy rain was forecast for Thursday afternoon, potentially affecting search efforts. Another adjacent building remained standing but had its wall sheared off, exposing interior rooms.
events.micro_summary: At least eight people died when a three-storey New York City building collapsed near a construction site.
events.summary: A three-storey building in New York City collapsed Wednesday afternoon at a construction site, killing at least eight people and injuring 17, including three firefighters, as rescuers dug through rubble for survivors.

events.extended_summary: A gunman opened fire at the Vida Fitness Gym in Washington DC's Logan Circle neighbourhood, shooting at least five people and killing one. The victim was the building manager. Another person was left in critical condition. The suspect, a physician in his 50s who had been in conflict with his homeowners' association, fled to a seventh-floor apartment believed to be his own and barricaded himself inside. Police forced the door open after hearing a gunshot and found the gunman dead from a self-inflicted wound. A fire had been set in the apartment building but was extinguished. The suspect had fired shots toward police through a door, forcing SWAT team members to temporarily retreat. Authorities evacuated buildings and urged people to stay away from the area before lifting the shelter-in-place order.
events.micro_summary: A gunman killed one person at a Washington DC gym before shooting himself dead.
events.summary: A gunman opened fire at a Washington DC gym, killing one person and wounding at least four others, before barricading himself in a nearby apartment and shooting himself dead, police said.

events.extended_summary: Moment teen rescued after six days in Australian bush A teenager missing for six days in dense Australian bushland has been found alive. William, whose surname has not been released, disappeared last Friday while on a camping trip with a friend in bushland about 180km (112 miles) east of Melbourne, Victoria. Extremely cold overnight temperatures had left authorities concerned for the 17-year-old's welfare. Police dogs, divers and helicopters had been involved in the search. He was located on Thursday morning and reunited with his relieved family, who said he was uninjured but "grounded for life". Rescuers winched William to safety, and fed him a doughnut and a bottle of water, before he was taken to hospital for a check up. events.extended_summary: The woman disappeared while on the Marella Voyager (file photo) A British woman has gone missing from a cruise ship while it was crossing the Atlantic, travel operator Tui has said. The 72-year-old was last seen aboard Tui's Marella Voyager on Monday while the vessel was en route to the Caribbean. The ship could have travelled hundreds of miles in the time between when she was last seen to when she was reported missing. Staff realised the passenger was missing on Tuesday, when they noticed her bed had not been slept in. The alarm was raised and a search carried out, Tui said in a statement. It is understood the missing guest was then reported to the US Coast Guard, which asked the ship to continue to its crossing rather than reverse course and search for the woman. events.extended_summary: India's consumer price index-based retail inflation rose to 6.09 percent year-on-year in October 2026, marking the highest level recorded during the year and breaching the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit of 6 percent. The headline inflation rate was higher in rural areas at 6.63 percent compared with 5.41 percent in urban areas. Food inflation surged to 8.94 percent year-on-year, with rural food inflation at 9.09 percent and urban at 8.68 percent. On a month-on-month basis, the all-India CPI increased 0.51 percent between September and October. The RBI targets inflation at 4 percent with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 percent. Market participants are pricing a 69 percent probability of a 25 basis point rate hike and 31 percent chance of a 50 basis point increase at the next monetary policy meeting, partly due to higher crude oil prices linked to the US-Iran war.
events.micro_summary: India's retail inflation hit 6.09% in October 2026, breaching the central bank's 6% tolerance limit.
events.summary: India's year-on-year retail inflation reached 6.09% in October 2026, the highest in 2026 and above the Reserve Bank of India's 6% upper tolerance limit, driven by food inflation of 8.94%.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend has crossed the Rs 500 crore mark at the domestic box office within its first week of release. The film, which arrived in theatres on November 5, collected Rs 511.10 crore nett domestically by Day 7. It opened with Rs 64.85 crore on Thursday, dipped to Rs 48.05 crore on Friday, then surged to Rs 69.80 crore on Saturday and Rs 56.15 crore on Sunday. Monday marked its biggest day with Rs 107.50 crore, a 91.5 per cent jump, followed by Rs 94.10 crore on Tuesday and Rs 70.65 crore on Wednesday. Its worldwide gross stands at Rs 934.55 crore. Mounted on a budget of Rs 4,000 crore, the film is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and stars Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Sunny Deol, Ravi Dubey and Lara Dutta.

events.extended_summary: Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal addressed the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam on Thursday, urging global businesses to invest in India and make it their address for factories, design centres and global capability centres. He pitched India as a safe and trusted destination for foreign direct investment amid global economic uncertainties and ongoing conflicts, citing Moody's upgraded FY27 growth estimate of 7% driven by robust consumption and strong macroeconomic fundamentals. Goyal assured investors that India would fully respect and protect intellectual property rights and never steal technology, emphasizing that trust is the scarcest commodity in the 21st century. He highlighted India's skilled youth contributing significantly to GDP growth and invited entrepreneurs to invest in manufacturing, tourism and other sectors, noting Visakhapatnam's transformation from a Steel City to a Silicon City.
events.micro_summary: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal pitched India as a safe investment destination with 7% growth forecast at Visakhapatnam summit.
events.summary: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal addressed the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam, urging global businesses to invest in India as a safe destination amid global uncertainties, citing Moody's 7% FY27 growth estimate and promising intellectual property protection.

events.extended_summary: OpenAI has introduced API inference residency in India, enabling eligible businesses to process supported GPT-6 Luna workloads entirely within the country. The service supports the model through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs, with both processing and customer data storage taking place in India. This move addresses data localisation requirements that have hindered AI adoption among regulated businesses such as banks, financial institutions, and government agencies. To use the offering, customers must create a new API project, select India as the location for both data storage and processing, and use the corresponding India regional endpoint. India joins Australia and Japan as markets where OpenAI has introduced API inference residency. The development extends OpenAI's existing data residency options in India, initially introduced in May 2025, and aims to help organisations move from experimenting with AI to deploying it in daily operations.
events.micro_summary: OpenAI launched API inference residency in India for GPT-6 Luna workloads to meet data localisation requirements.
events.summary: OpenAI introduced API inference residency in India, allowing eligible businesses to process GPT-6 Luna workloads and store data within the country to address data localisation requirements for regulated industries.

events.extended_summary: Durga Rao Tompaki will lead a 17-member visually challenged Indian cricket team to the Asia Cup in Dhaka, scheduled from November 15 to 20. The BCCI is sponsoring round-trip air tickets from New Delhi to Dhaka for the squad, which includes players from Gujarat, Delhi, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana and Karnataka. India will open their campaign against Sri Lanka on November 15, face Pakistan on November 17, and take on hosts Bangladesh on November 19, with the final scheduled for November 20. India, who won the title a decade ago, will be looking to reclaim the trophy. The team was given a send-off in New Delhi organized by the Cricket Association for the Blind in India in association with Samarthanam Trust and CBRE, whose CSR initiative Ek Pehal supported preparations including coaching, nutrition, fitness, physiotherapy, travel and equipment.
events.micro_summary: Durga Rao Tompaki leads 17-member visually challenged Indian cricket team to Asia Cup in Dhaka November 15-20.
events.summary: Durga Rao Tompaki will captain a 17-member visually challenged Indian team at the Asia Cup in Dhaka November 15-20, with BCCI sponsoring air travel. India opens against Sri Lanka November 15, then faces Pakistan and Bangladesh before November 20 final.

events.extended_summary: India's men's national football team suffered a 0-5 defeat to New Zealand in their first international friendly of the November FIFA window at Go Media Stadium in Auckland on Thursday. New Zealand opened the scoring in the fifth minute through an own goal by Bijoy Varghese, before Jesse Randall struck twice to make it 3-0 at half-time. Chris Wood headed in the fourth goal in the 57th minute and Lachlan Bayliss scored from a volley in the 74th minute to complete the rout. India goalkeeper Vishal Kaith was a standout performer, making several crucial saves including a penalty from Bill Tuiloma in the 78th minute to prevent a bigger defeat. The loss extends India's poor run, having conceded 15 goals in their last three fixtures. Both teams will meet again in Christchurch on Sunday.
events.micro_summary: India suffered 0-5 defeat to New Zealand in Auckland friendly.
events.summary: India lost 0-5 to New Zealand in Auckland friendly, with goals from an own goal, Jesse Randall's brace, Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss; goalkeeper Vishal Kaith saved a penalty.

events.extended_summary: At least 14 people were killed and six others injured on Thursday when a microbus plunged down a hilly road in Nepal's Bagmati province. The accident occurred around 5:45 am in the Makawanpur district when the vehicle, carrying around 17 people, plunged approximately 300 metres down a hilly section of the Bhimfedi-Kulekhani-Kathmandu road in Bhimfedi Rural Municipality. The vehicle was travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi. The driver was among those killed, and six injured passengers were admitted to a local hospital in Hetauda Municipality for treatment. The passengers were residents of Sarlahi district returning from Kathmandu to celebrate the Hindu festival Chhath, which falls on Sunday. A seven-member rescue team was deployed to the accident site.
events.micro_summary: At least 14 people died when a microbus plunged down a hilly road in Nepal's Bagmati province.
events.summary: A microbus carrying around 17 people plunged 300 metres down a hilly road in Nepal's Makawanpur district at 5:45 am Thursday, killing at least 14 and injuring six while travelling from Kathmandu to Sarlahi.
